newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids steady to down with crude, gas.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids steady to down with crude, gas.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices were unchanged to down slightly Monday in sluggish trade, but sentiment grew more bearish as mild weather took its toll on gas and prospects for renewed Iraqi exports weighed on crude.

"It's still early in the season, but we're looking at a mild week, and Iraq was on people's minds," said one cash trader, referring to news the U.N. Secretary General approved the start of an oil-for-food deal that will enable Iraq to return to the world oil market for the first time since 1990. In New York Harbor, physical one percent was unchanged at $22.50-75 a barrel, traders said.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour notionally held steady at $23.00-25, while low pour was off a quarter to $24.50-75.
High sulphurs in NYH again were unchanged to modestly lower, with three percent notionally down 25-50 cents to $18.50-75.
Traders said a spate of refinery problems like Star's damaged H-oil unit in Louisiana were likely to keep HSFO on the defensive near-term.
At the U.S. Gulf Coast, one percent was stable at $19.75, while three percent slipped 25 cents to $16.50 or lower.
No NYH or USG deals were reported.
New York city gate gas prices tumbled more than 20 cents Monday to about $4.20/mmBtu, still well-above NYH one percent resid at a $3.59/mmBtu equivalent.
